newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan king pledges to end Iraq smuggling.
newsitem.headline: Jordan king pledges to end Iraq smuggling.

text.p: Jordan's King Hussein pledged during a tour of the kingdom's border area with Iraq on Thursday to put more effort into stamping out smuggling.

"Everything that enters this land and gets out of it should enter and go out through legal channels," King Hussein told the Bedouin forces who police Jordan's long desert borders with Iraq, Syria and Saudi Arabia.
"Our responsibility from now on is to ensure implementing this within our maximum efforts and resources," he told them in an address shown on state-run Jordan Television.
Jordanian nomadic tribes have a flourishing trade in smuggled livestock, bought cheaply from Iraqi herdsmen.

But most smuggling into Iraq has ended since 1992 when Jordan tightened its border regime under U.S. pressure to comply with a U.N. trade embargo on Baghdad imposed for Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
King Hussein also pledged during the tour of area near Iraq's border crossing that a shortage of manpower to patrol the vast areas would be solved "very soon". He also promised new equipment.

Jordan has recently intensified a campaign against drug smuggling, with police announcing large hauls along the Iraqi and Saudi borders. The king said one member of the border patrol was killed while chasing smugglers on Tuesday.
Jordan is a major transit route for the drug trade between Turkey, Syria and Saudi Arabia.
